description: Fig. 6 is a 3-row × 4-column composite grid comparing segmentation outputs. Rows are labelled 'Image' (raw input), 'MatSAM' (proposed model) and 'Specialist' (data-specific model); columns are labelled (a) NBS-2, (b) AZA, (c) UHCS and (d) LCS. (a) is a grayscale SEM/BSE image of dark irregular precipitates in a lighter fine-dotted matrix; both result rows render the precipitates white on black, with pink/magenta marking under-segmentation and cyan/blue over-segmentation, and small yellow arrows flagging precipitates that MatSAM recovers where the specialist under-segments. (b) is a grayscale XCT image of a dark AlZn dendrite inside a circular region; both masks extract it as white shapes on black. (c) is a dark, rough SEM surface densely covered by light spheroidite particles; masks overlay pink particles on a brown background, and MatSAM marks visibly many more particles than the Specialist row. (d) is a polycrystalline optical micrograph of light grains with dark boundaries, and both result rows reproduce the grain-boundary network. No scale bars, axis labels or numeric values are printed anywhere; the figure is qualitative, arguing that MatSAM matches or exceeds specialist models without training, most clearly on small blurred precipitates.
measured_quantities: segmentation IoU (dimensionless; reported in the text/Table 3, not printed in the figure)

observations.observation: The figure is a 3-row × 4-column grid; rows are labelled 'Image', 'MatSAM' and 'Specialist', and columns are lettered (a)-(d).
Column (a) raw input is a grayscale micrograph with dark, irregular precipitates of several size classes in a lighter matrix, identified in the caption as NBS-2.
In column (a) the Specialist mask contains an orange triangular marker and lacks several precipitates that appear white in the MatSAM mask, which is annotated with small yellow arrows.
Column (b) is a grayscale XCT image of a dark dendrite inside a circular region (AZA), and both result rows extract it as white shapes on a black background.
Column (c) shows a dark rough SEM surface densely populated by light spheroidite particles; the MatSAM mask overlays many more pink particle masks on the brown background than the Specialist mask.
Column (d) is an optical micrograph of polycrystalline grains with dark boundaries, and both result rows reproduce essentially the same grain-boundary network.
The first row shows open-sourced images: (a) NBS-2 [16], (b) AZA [25], (c) UHCS [11] and (d) LCS [11].
The caption states that the second row displays MatSAM results and the third row the data-specific (specialist) models, with the mask images cropped from the raw figures of the respective articles.
The caption states that pink and blue represent under- and over-segmentation respectively for (a) and (b), while for (c) pink areas are the masks.
MatSAM scores IoU 0.82 on NBS-2, 3.0 % higher than the specialist model, and 0.91 on NBS-1.
On AZA, MatSAM reaches an IoU of 0.96 versus 0.97 for the corresponding specialist model trained on over 1000 annotated samples.
On UHCS, MatSAM attains 0.76, outperforming the specialist model by 5.0 %, while SAM, OTSU and Adaptive obtain 0.58, 0.56 and 0.46.

For polycrystalline LCS images, the citing text states that MatSAM shows comparable recognition performance to the original method without human intervention, and LCS is analysed qualitatively because released labels are lacking.

subfigures.description: Raw grayscale SEM/BSE image (NBS-2) of dark, irregular, blocky precipitates of differing sizes in a lighter matrix with fine dotted texture. MatSAM and Specialist rows give white-on-black precipitate masks; pink/magenta = under-segmentation, cyan/blue = over-segmentation; yellow arrows point to precipitates MatSAM segments that the Specialist misses, and the Specialist mask carries an orange triangular marker.

Raw grayscale XCT image (AZA) of a dark AlZn dendrite located centrally within a circular region on a lighter gray background. Both MatSAM and Specialist masks show the dendrite as white shapes on black; only a few small pink/cyan fragments are visible in the MatSAM mask.

Raw grayscale SEM image (UHCS) of a rough alloy crack surface densely and uniformly covered by light-coloured spheroidite particles on a dark background. Result rows overlay pink masks on a brown background; MatSAM labels a much denser set of particles than the Specialist row, which leaves many particles unmasked.

Optical micrograph (LCS) of polycrystalline grains: large light grains separated by dark grain boundaries. Both MatSAM and Specialist rows reconstruct the same grain-boundary network as black lines on white grains.

unreadable_items: No scale bars, magnification values, axis labels or numeric value labels are printed on any panel
Small pink/cyan over-/under-segmentation fragments in the (a) and (b) masks are too small to attribute to individual features at the supplied resolution
